REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - FEBRUARY 22, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
FEBRUARY 22, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was led by Bishop David Montgomery from The Church of Jesus
  Christ of Latter-Day Saints.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by City of Cerritos Recreation Services
  Division, Youth Basketball League Girls Pee Wee Team - Avalanche.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations

  Leelin Bakery and Café (Business Spotlight).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Chris Foster expressed concerns  regarding  an  Economic  Development

  Angel Soto inquired as to the Council’s position regarding Councilmember term

  Afshan Abbas inquired about a phone call she received from Cerritos High

  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of an appeal by project applicant MLC Holdings Inc. of the
  Planning Commission decision (Planning Commission Resolution No. 2018-2) denying
  a proposal for a proposed 24-unit detached single-family residential development
  (9.48 dwelling units per acre) on an existing fully-developed and improved property
  located at 13017 Artesia Boulevard (APN 7008-004-033), currently zoned
  commercial office professional (COP), and all related entitlements, including
  Development Code Amendment 2017-7, General Plan Amendment 2017-2,
  Development Map Amendment 2017-3, vesting Tentative Tract Map 75009, Precise
  Plan 2017-13, and Community Facilities District 2017-1 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager, Sandy
  Cisneros, Senior Planner, and Robert Lopez, Current Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Lester Tucker, applicant/appellant, Vice President, MLC Holdings, Inc., reported MLC
  Holdings has chosen to appeal the Planning Commission's decision as they feel it is
  inconsistent with the stated goals of the City's General Plan and Housing Element.
  The project presents a rare opportunity to enhance the City's housing stock and
  bring in new families and home ownership opportunities to Cerritos. He highlighted
  findings that support approval of the project and stated the plan incorporates the
  feedback received from the Planning Commission, staff and residents. Mr. Tucker
  reported staff never supported RS-5000 for this project and supports it, without it.
  He listed some of the changes they have made to accommodate neighbors and
  referenced 73 letters of support and 30 letters of opposition, as provided in the
  agenda packet. He urged Council to consider the appeal and reverse the Planning
  Commission’s denial.

  Seema Gupta spoke in opposition to the project with concerns regarding the
  proposed number of houses, increased traffic, and the lack of space for children to
  play.

  Marlene Rofe stated she was pleased the developer added an exit driveway on
  Artesia Boulevard and expressed concerns regarding access for trash pickup, mail
  carriers, and emergency and delivery vehicles.

  Sam Desai spoke in opposition to the project, noting it has been reviewed multiple
  times by the Planning Commission, was denied, and the developer has offered
  nothing new.
 City of Cerritos  February 22, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Marianne Hughlett spoke in opposition to the project, noting concerns with
  congestion and increased traffic, and adding that if Council decides to approve the
  project, a traffic signal should be installed between Shoemaker and Carmenita.

  Diana Coronado, Building Industry Association, spoke in support of the project,
  adding that MLC Holdings has gone above and beyond to address the Planning
  Commission's concerns as well as residents' concerns. She noted the need for
  increased housing in the State and urged Council to approve the project.

  Steven Shin spoke in support of the project and stated his family would jump at the
  opportunity to buy a new home such as proposed by MLC Holdings.

  Charlie Joslin noted the Planning Commission spoke against the project with
  concerns regarding the density and removal of mature trees.  He spoke in
  opposition to the project and urged Council to vote against it.

  Scott Smith, President and CEO, Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce, reported
  receiving no donations from the developer but stated they are dues-paying
  members and have sponsored two Chamber events. He commented on the
  Chamber's mission and goal and spoke in support of the project. He noted new
  families will shop, dine and possibly work in Cerritos and will make the economy
  stronger.

  Chung Fu Luan spoke in opposition of the project and wondered how the proposal
  came forward without prior approval of a zoning change. He opined there should
  have been several alternatives in the environmental assessment including a "no
  build" option. He reported neighbors oppose the project because of possible
  negative impacts to privacy, increased density and noted the project is not
  compatible, nor consistent, with the neighborhood.

  Carol Rayburn stated the City is becoming stagnant, in terms of the housing
  presented to those who want to live in Cerritos. She commented on the need for
  diversification in the types of housing provided for residents, a diminishing student
  population and on the lack of housing stock for sale. She spoke in support of the
  project noting it will bring new families into the City and will stimulate the housing
  market.

  Celia Spitzer reported on her experience as a Planning Commissioner and as a
  member and Chair of her Homeowners Association Architectural Committee. She
  spoke in opposition to the project noting it does not meet the standards of the City.
  She encouraged Council to uphold the decision of the Planning Commission and
  deny the appeal, and listed reasons for doing so.

  Gail Grossman spoke in opposition to the project and listed concerns related to
  traffic congestion, lack of open space, proximity of houses to each other, decreased
  privacy, lack of guest parking, impacts on first responders and the lack of areas for
  children to play. She alleged Planning Commission Chair Bui does not live in
  Cerritos and urged Council to uphold the Planning Commission's decision and deny
  the appeal.
 City of Cerritos  February 22, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)
8A.  (continued)

  Mark Anthony Ruiz immediate past-president of Rancho SE Association of Realtors,
  read a letter on behalf of the current president, Pedro Aceituno, requesting approval
  of the Juliet project.

  Dr. Afshan Abbas expressed concerns regarding increased traffic congestion and
  offered to provide video evidence of how bad traffic is in the area. She commented
  on limited access for utility and emergency vehicles in the complex and on the lack
  of guest parking. She urged Council to uphold the Planning Commission decision
  and deny the appeal.

  Daisy (last name not provided) thanked the Mayor for her leadership and spoke in
  opposition to the Juliet project. She urged Council to listen to residents and uphold
  the decision of the Planning Commission and deny the appeal.

  Moses Kim, MLC Holdings, Inc., referenced the City's traffic study noting it resulted
  in 49% less traffic in the area. He listed the changes made in response to
  residents' comments and claimed to deny this project is denying an opportunity for
  24 new families to own homes in Cerritos.

  Charles McKeag, President, MLC Holdings, reported California is under siege by
  failing to produce enough housing to support its own weight. He noted most
  residents have had the opportunity at the "American Dream" and addressed the
  importance of allowing the next generation the same opportunity. He urged
  Council to do its part and approve the appeal.

  Kat Joslin stated it should speak volumes that so many residents have shown up at
  every meeting considering this project. She commented on a meeting set up by
  the developer, and stated trust has been compromised. She addressed the
  Planning Commission's reasons for denying the project and urged Council to uphold
  the Planning Commission's decision and deny the appeal.

  C.W. Van der Linden spoke in opposition to the project with concerns regarding
  increased traffic congestion, increased water usage, questioned if there is a
  shortage of housing and affordability of the proposed homes. He urged Council to
  deny the appeal.

  Mel Cortez commented on the developer's efforts to lobby for the project and on
  the money spent to "push" it. He spoke in opposition to the project noting it is not
  consistent with the City's standards and urged Council to deny the appeal.

  Rod and Judi Dixon spoke in opposition to the project, expressed pride at residents
  of Cerritos who have provided their input, and urged Council to listen to the
  residents and deny the appeal.

  Jimmy Sakoda noted residents oppose the project with similar concerns, expressed
  his opposition the project, felt the changes made by the developer are not enough,
  and urged Council to deny the appeal.
 City of Cerritos  February 22, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)
8A.  (continued)

  Anantha Ramachandran opposed the project, noted the high-density zoning does
  not fit with the surrounding neighborhood and urged Council to uphold the Planning
  Commission's decision and deny the appeal.

  Jerome Jenson expressed concerns regarding the proposed density, emergency
  vehicle access, existing trees and setting a precedent.

  Sue Carter spoke in favor of the project and in support of change, noted the
  housing shortages in the State, and urged Council to consider what is best for the
  City.

  Jacque Kline spoke about her experience living near Shoemaker and Artesia,
  expressed concerns with traffic and lack of space for children to play and spoke in
  opposition to the project.

  Jennifer Pilapil opined the proposed project does not fit into the neighborhood,
  spoke in favor of mixed uses with residential over retail uses and urged Council to
  deny the appeal.

  Robert Sampo expressed concerns with access for emergency vehicles in the
  proposed project, commented on the Planning Commission's consideration and
  denial of the project and urged Council to uphold their decision and deny the
  appeal.

  Jay Gray spoke in opposition to the project, commented on the Planning
  Commission's consideration and recommendation, and urged Council to deny the
  appeal.

  Daniel Fierro read a letter on behalf of ABC Unified School District Trustee Chris
  Apodaca in support of the project.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to waive full reading of
  and adopt Resolution No. 2018-03, A RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY
  COUNCIL  UPHOLDING  THE  PLANNING  COMMISSION  DECISION
  (PLANNING COMMISSION RESOLUTION NO. 2018-2) DENYING A
  PROPOSAL FOR A PROPOSED 24-UNIT DETACHED SINGLE-FAMILY
  RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT (9.48 DWELLING UNITS PER ACRE) ON AN
  EXISTING FULLY-DEVELOPED AND IMPROVED PROPERTY LOCATED AT
  13017 ARTESIA BOULEVARD (APN 7008-004-033), CURRENTLY ZONED
  COMMERCIAL OFFICE PROFESSIONAL (COP), AND ALL RELATED
  ENTITLEMENTS, INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2017-7,
  GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT 2017-2, DEVELOPMENT MAP AMENDMENT
  2017-3, VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP 75009, PRECISE PLAN 2017-13,
  AND COMMUNITY FACILITIES DISTRICT 2017-1 (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  February 22, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  Edwards
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of a contract for design of traffic signal

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract
